title: Distortion of AI Alignment Revisited: RLHF is a Decent Utilitarian Aligner
claim: Distortion stays tightly bounded across regimes of the regularization budget, with matching upper and lower bounds showing where degradation arises.
layout: 1 panel, plot with shaded regions; piecewise curve, labeled theorem regions
description: A single schematic plot of distortion (y-axis) against KL budget τ (x-axis) with no numeric values. A thick black piecewise curve is flat at a low level on the left, rises steeply to a plateau, then declines along a curve and levels off at a low value on the right. Each segment is labeled with its asymptotic distortion: O(e^B)^τ on the rise, Θ(βB) on the plateau, O(βB)τ^-1 on the decline, and Θ(β) on the right tail. Above the curve a pink region is labeled 'Theorem 4.1 (upper bound)'. A blue region below the curve is labeled 'Theorem 5.1 (RLHF lower bound)'. Gray regions at the bottom left and bottom right are labeled 'Theorem 5.2 (alg. indep. lower bound)'. Dotted vertical lines mark thresholds Θ(1), Θ(B) and e^{-Θ(B)}. The eye goes first to the bold red and blue theorem labels.
caption: Overview of the upper and lower bounds in the analysis in the AI alignment setting (with the KL constraint), shown for a given distribution mismatch B.
abstract: While Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback (RLHF) is the standard paradigm for aligning large language models with human preferences, its effectiveness in pluralistic settings has been called into question. Notably, recent work by GÃ¶lz et al. (2025) demonstrated that the \textit{distortion} -- defined as the multiplicative gap between the average user utility of the RLHF policy and the optimal average utility -- can scale exponentially with the Bradley-Terry temperature parameter $Î²$ when users have heterogeneous preferences. In this work, we present a fine-grained analysis of the distortion of RLHF with reward clipping and demonstrate that such exponential degradation is not a fundamental property of the algorithm but rather a consequence of distribution mismatch between the distribution generating preference data ($Î¼$) and the KL reference policy ($Ï_{\mathrm{ref}}$). To this end, we establish tight upper and lower bounds on the distortion of RLHF across multiple regimes of the KL regularization strength. We show that in a representative regime, under the Bradley-Terry model, the distortion is $\tildeÎ(Î²B + Î²)$, where $B$ is an upper bound on the log density ratio between $Î¼$ and $Ï_{\mathrm{ref}}$. In particular, when there is no distribution mismatch (i.e., $Î¼= Ï_{\mathrm{ref}}$), RLHF achieves the optimal distortion of $O(Î²)$ up to a constant. Our results suggest that, to reasonably maximize average utility with RLHF, it is preferable to use on-policy sampled preference data or to fine-tune before RLHF on data from a source close to $Î¼$.
